title: 日本語総まとめ N1 文法

items.q: その国で生活（ ）文化がわかるというものだ。
items.qr: Sono kuni de seikatsu (___) bunka ga wakaru to iu mono da.
items.en: It is only by living in that country that you come to understand its culture.
items.why: 〜てこそ always attaches to the te-form, never the ta-form — したこそ simply isn't a grammatical option in this slot.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 1 · 感謝こそすれ

items.q: 程度の違いこそ（ ）、悪いことをしたのは皆同じだ。
items.qr: Teido no chigai koso (___), warui koto o shita no wa mina onaji da.
items.en: Although there's a difference in degree, everyone did something bad all the same.
items.why: 違い is a noun describing an existing state, which pairs with こそあれ. こそすれ is reserved for asserting a fact while denying its opposite — there's no such denial here, so it doesn't fit.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 1 · 感謝こそすれ

items.q: 彼は字（ ）汚いが、いい文章を書く。
items.qr: Kare wa ji (___) kitanai ga, ii bunshou o kaku.
items.en: His handwriting is admittedly messy, but he writes good essays.
items.why: This is a simple "X is true, but Y" contrast (字こそ汚いが) — pattern 4's job. こそすれ would need a denial-of-the-opposite structure, which isn't what's happening here.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 1 · 感謝こそすれ

items.q: ここは、（ ）こそあれ、緑が多くていいところだ。
items.qr: Koko wa, (___) koso are, midori ga ookute ii tokoro da.
items.en: This place is admittedly inconvenient, but it's got a lot of greenery and is a nice spot.
items.why: 〜こそあれ needs the な-adjective's て-form (で), not its attributive な-form — 不便な directly before こそあれ is ungrammatical.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 1 · 感謝こそすれ

items.q: 文章は理解（ ）意味がある。
items.qr: Bunshou wa rikai (___) imi ga aru.
items.en: A piece of writing only has meaning once/if it is understood.
items.why: This is 〜てこそ again (point 1) — こそ must follow the completed te-form (passive されて), never sit in front of it.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 1 · 感謝こそすれ

items.q: たぶん行けないと思うので、私はいない（ ）話を進めてください。
items.qr: Tabun ikenai to omou node, watashi wa inai (___) hanashi o susumete kudasai.
items.en: I probably won't be able to go, so please proceed treating me as absent.
items.why: ものとして treats a premise ("I'm not there") as given; 人として means "as a person/in one's capacity as a human being," which doesn't fit "assume I'm absent."
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · できるものとして

items.q: 愛する人が病気で苦しむのを見るくらいなら、（ ）。
items.qr: Aisuru hito ga byouki de kurushimu no o miru kurai nara, (___).
items.en: Rather than watch someone I love suffer from illness, I'd rather get sick myself.

opts.en: better not to look (doesn't resolve the comparison)

opts.t: 自分が病気になったほうがいい
opts.r: jibun ga byouki ni natta hou ga ii

items.why: くらいなら needs a genuine alternative action in the following clause; "not looking" doesn't actually replace the situation, while "getting sick myself" is a real (if extreme) alternative — exactly the shape this pattern needs.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · できるものとして

items.q: 転勤でそんな田舎に行かされる（ ）、会社を辞めたほうがいい。
items.qr: Tenkin de sonna inaka ni ikasareru (___), kaisha o yameta hou ga ii.
items.en: Rather than be transferred to such a rural place, it's better to quit the company.

opts.en: because it's the case that (wrong logic)

items.why: The sentence sets up a rejected option (being transferred) against a preferred one (quitting) — exactly くらいなら's job. ものだから gives a reason/cause, which doesn't fit this "rather than" comparison.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · できるものとして

items.q: ぼくが買える家は、これ（ ）。
items.qr: Boku ga kaeru ie wa, kore (___).
items.en: The house I can afford is only this much (i.e. this level).
items.why: This is the fixed pattern 〜ぐらいのものだ (limiting scope to "only this"); ぐらいにしたものだ isn't a recognized grammatical form.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · できるものとして

items.q: 契約の期限が来た場合には、新たに契約書を交わす（ ）。
items.qr: Keiyaku no kigen ga kita baai ni wa, arata ni keiyakusho o kawasu (___).
items.en: When the contract term expires, a new contract shall be exchanged.
items.why: This is a formal contract clause, exactly the register ものとする is built for; ものになる just means "it turns into something," which doesn't fit stipulating a rule.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 2 · できるものとして

items.q: お互いが助け合うこと（ ）、人間は生きていけない。
items.qr: Otagai ga tasukeau koto (___), ningen wa ikite ikenai.
items.en: Humans cannot survive without helping one another.
items.why: The sentence needs "without helping each other, survival is impossible" — a condition, not a reason; ことなしに supplies exactly that, while ことだから would just restate helping each other as a cause.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 3 · 彼のことだから

items.q: 明るい彼女のこと（ ）、どこへ行ってもすぐ友達ができるだろう。
items.qr: Akarui kanojo no koto (___), doko e itte mo sugu tomodachi ga dekiru darou.
items.en: Since she's such a cheerful person, she'll surely make friends quickly wherever she goes.
items.why: This is Point 3's Nのことだから — basing a confident prediction ("she'll make friends easily") on her known cheerful personality.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 3 · 彼のことだから

items.q: 兄が書いたレポートを、自分が（ ）提出した。
items.qr: Ani ga kaita repooto o, jibun ga (___) teishutsu shita.
items.en: He submitted the report his older brother wrote, pretending he had written it himself.
items.why: This is exactly Point 5's "treat as contrary to fact" — claiming authorship that isn't true; ことなしに would mean "without writing it," which contradicts submitting a written report at all.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 3 · 彼のことだから

items.q: 道に（ ）、前もって地図で場所を確かめておいた。
items.qr: Michi ni (___), maemotte chizu de basho o tashikamete oita.
items.en: So as not to get lost, I checked the location on a map beforehand.

opts.t: 迷うことのないように
opts.r: mayou koto no nai you ni
opts.en: so as not to get lost

items.why: The sentence is a precaution taken beforehand ("checked the map so as not to get lost"), which is Point 1's job; ことなしに instead states a condition for a result, which doesn't fit "checked a map in advance."
items.unit: Week 1 Day 3 · 彼のことだから

items.q: 彼女は今まで苦労（ ）ことなしに生きてきた。
items.qr: Kanojo wa ima made kurou (___) koto nashi ni ikite kita.
items.en: She has lived without ever experiencing hardship.

opts.en: plain non-past (correct form before ことなしに)

items.why: Like 〜てこそ from Day 1, 〜ことなしに attaches to the plain non-past form even when describing a state that has held true up to now — 苦労することなしに, not 苦労したことなしに.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 3 · 彼のことだから

items.q: 新しいロケットの完成が（ ）。
items.qr: Atarashii roketto no kansei ga (___).
items.en: The completion of the new rocket is eagerly awaited.

opts.en: is made to wait (ordinary causative-passive, wrong subject)
is eagerly awaited (自発の受身形)

items.why: Point 2's られる describes the completion being (spontaneously/naturally) awaited; 待たされます would mean a person is being made to wait by someone — the wrong picture entirely.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · 私に言わせれば

items.q: 彼は社会人として必要（ ）知識に欠ける。
items.qr: Kare wa shakaijin toshite hitsuyou (___) chishiki ni kakeru.
items.en: He lacks the knowledge considered necessary for a working member of society.
items.why: "Knowledge considered necessary" is a social consensus, exactly Point 1's とされる; にしている would mean someone actively makes something into X, which doesn't fit describing widely-held knowledge standards.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · 私に言わせれば

items.q: 我々の世代の人間に（ ）、彼の行動は普通ではない。
items.qr: Wareware no sedai no ningen ni (___), kare no koudou wa futsuu de wa nai.
items.en: As far as people of our generation are concerned, his behavior isn't normal.

opts.en: if you ask, in the opinion of
if (something) is said (ordinary passive conditional, wrong fit)

items.why: Point 4's Nに言わせれば introduces "in N's opinion"; 言われれば is just the ordinary passive conditional of 言う ("if it's said") and doesn't attach the intended "opinion-holder" meaning to 我々の世代の人間に.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · 私に言わせれば

items.q: それは、死について真剣に（ ）映画だった。
items.qr: Sore wa, shi ni tsuite shinken ni (___) eiga datta.
items.en: It was a movie that made me seriously think about death.

opts.en: made to think, cannot help but think

items.why: This is Point 3's causative-passive 考えさせられる — the movie (external trigger) provokes reflection the viewer couldn't help; 考えされる simply isn't a correctly formed verb.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · 私に言わせれば

items.q: この新薬は、効果はあるが、副作用が強い（ ）。
items.qr: Kono shinyaku wa, kouka wa aru ga, fukusayou ga tsuyoi (___).
items.en: This new drug is effective, but is said to have strong side effects.

opts.en: (treated as if — wrong pattern for a claimed fact)

items.why: This reports an accepted medical claim — Point 1's とされている; Day 3's ことにされている would imply the side effects are being fictitiously treated as strong contrary to fact, which isn't the intended meaning here.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 4 · 私に言わせれば

items.q: もし車を買い換える（ ）、次はドイツの車がほしい。
items.qr: Moshi kuruma o kaikaeru (___), tsugi wa doitsu no kuruma ga hoshii.
items.en: If I were to replace my car, I'd want a German car next.
items.why: もし ("if") signals a pure hypothetical, which is とすれば's job; とみると would need an actual perceived trigger, not a hypothetical もし-clause.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 難しいとみると…

items.q: 彼女は苦労した（ ）、実際の年齢より老けて見える。
items.qr: Kanojo wa kurou shita (___), jissai no nenrei yori fukete mieru.
items.en: She seems to have had a hard life, as she looks older than her actual age.

opts.en: as, in the capacity of (wrong pattern)

items.why: "Looking older than her age" is the evidence the speaker uses to infer she's had a hard life — exactly とみえて's job; として just means "as/in the role of," which doesn't fit an inference at all.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 難しいとみると…

items.q: 彼女の普段の成績から、合格は間違いないと（ ）。
items.qr: Kanojo no fudan no seiseki kara, goukaku wa machigainai to (___).
items.en: Judging from her usual grades, she is expected to pass without question.
items.why: "Based on her grades, she's expected to pass" is an impersonal, evidence-based forecast — Point 2's とみられる; とみえている isn't how this pattern is used (とみえる doesn't take みえている as a fixed form here).
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 難しいとみると…

items.q: 彼は、女性が地方出身だ（ ）すぐに声をかける。
items.qr: Kare wa, josei ga chihou shusshin da (___) sugu ni koe o kakeru.
items.en: As soon as he notices a woman is from the countryside, he approaches her.
items.why: This describes a real, repeated habitual reaction the instant he perceives something — Point 3's とみると; とすれば would turn it into a hypothetical, which doesn't fit a description of his actual behavior pattern.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 難しいとみると…

items.q: 彼が犯人（ ）、犯罪を犯した動機は何だろう。
items.qr: Kare ga hannin (___), hanzai o okashita douki wa nan darou.
items.en: If he is the culprit, what would be the motive for the crime?

opts.en: it seems (wrong — no evidence being cited)

items.why: This is a pure "if X, then what follows" reasoning chain about a hypothesis — Point 4's とすると; とみえて would need the speaker to be inferring from some observed evidence, which isn't what's happening here.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 5 · 難しいとみると…

items.q: どんなに（ ）、絶対に間に合わないだろう。
items.qr: Donna ni (___), zettai ni ma ni awanai darou.
items.en: No matter how much you run, you definitely won't make it in time.

opts.en: no matter how much one runs

items.why: どんなに ("no matter how") is the classic signal for Point 3's 〜たところで…ない; ところを would just mark a moment in time, not a futile effort.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 6 · 何回読んだところで…

items.q: お忙しい（ ）お集まりいただき、ありがとうございます。
items.qr: Oisogashii (___) oatsumari itadaki, arigatou gozaimasu.
items.en: Thank you for gathering here despite being busy.

opts.en: at a moment when (thanking for the state)
even if (wrong sense — no concession here)

items.why: This is the classic polite set phrase from Point 1 — thanking someone for their state (being busy) at the moment they came; ところで would turn it into a "no matter how busy" concession, which isn't a natural thank-you.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 6 · 何回読んだところで…

items.q: 「CDは月にどのくらい買うの。」「だいたい5枚（ ）ね。」
items.qr: "CD wa tsuki ni dono kurai kau no." "Daitai go-mai (___) ne."
items.en: "About how many CDs do you buy a month?" "About 5, I'd say."

opts.en: (missing the という that makes this an estimate)

items.why: A rough quantity estimate needs Point 2's full 〜というところだ; bare ところだ (without という) is a different, unrelated pattern meaning "just about to."
items.unit: Week 1 Day 6 · 何回読んだところで…

items.q: 彼の借金は、休みなく毎日働いた（ ）、返せるような額ではない。
items.qr: Kare no shakkin wa, yasumi naku mainichi hataraita (___), kaeseru you na gaku de wa nai.
items.en: His debt is not an amount that could be repaid even if he worked every day without rest.
items.why: "Working every day still isn't enough to repay it" is Point 3's "no matter how much V, negative result persists" — ところを would only mark a moment, not this futility.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 6 · 何回読んだところで…

items.q: あの頑固な父にタバコをやめさせよう（ ）、無駄だよ。
items.qr: Ano ganko na chichi ni tabako o yamesaseyou (___), muda da yo.
items.en: Even if you try to make that stubborn father of mine quit smoking, it's pointless.
items.why: Point 4 attaches to an attempted action (やめさせよう, volitional form + と) with と, not に — としたって is the correct concessive here.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 6 · 何回読んだところで…

items.q: 彼のゴルフの腕はなかなかのものだが、プロの（ ）、まだまだだ。
items.qr: Kare no gorufu no ude wa nakanaka no mono da ga, puro no (___), mada mada da.
items.en: His golfing skill is quite good, but from a pro's point of view, he's still got a long way to go.

opts.en: from my/a professional's point of view

items.why: Day 4's Nから言わせれば ("from N's point of view") fits perfectly — a pro's perspective contrasts with the layperson's positive impression.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: まじめな彼女（ ）、無断で休むということはないでしょう。
items.qr: Majime na kanojo (___), mudan de yasumu to iu koto wa nai deshou.
items.en: Since she's such a diligent person, she surely wouldn't skip work without notice.
items.why: Day 3's Nのことだから bases a confident prediction on her known diligent character.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: ぼくの貯金は（ ）、増えることはない。
items.qr: Boku no chokin wa (___), fueru koto wa nai.
items.en: My savings, if anything, only decrease — they never increase.

opts.t: 減ることのないように
opts.r: heru koto no nai you ni
opts.en: so as not to decrease (wrong sense)
if anything, decreases — certainly not the opposite

items.why: Week 1 Day 1's 〜こそすれ asserts a fact (savings decrease) while denying the opposite (increasing) — exactly this sentence's structure.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 無駄な道路工事をする（ ）減税してほしい。
items.qr: Muda na douro kouji o suru (___) genzei shite hoshii.
items.en: Rather than carrying out wasteful road construction, I'd want tax cuts.
items.why: Day 2's くらいなら rejects one action (wasteful construction) in favor of a preferred alternative (tax cuts).
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 練習（ ）、どんなスポーツも上達することはない。
items.qr: Renshuu (___), donna supootsu mo joutatsu suru koto wa nai.
items.en: Without practice, no sport ever improves.

opts.t: しなかったことにして
opts.en: pretending not to have done (wrong sense)

items.why: Day 3's ことなしに states the strict precondition (practice) needed for the result (improvement).
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 今年は消費税の値上げはない（ ）が、来年あたりはあるかもしれない。
items.qr: Kotoshi wa shouhizei no neage wa nai (___) ga, rainen atari wa aru kamo shirenai.
items.en: This year it's said there won't be a consumption-tax hike, but there might be one around next year.

opts.en: has become a thing where (wrong fit)

items.why: Day 4's とされる reports a widely-held claim (no tax hike this year) exactly as objective news commentary would.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: その会社は業績が悪い（ ）、あちこちの支店を閉店した。
items.qr: Sono kaisha wa gyouseki ga warui (___), achikochi no shiten o heiten shita.
items.en: The company's performance seems bad, as it has closed branches here and there.
items.why: Day 5's とみえて infers bad performance from the visible evidence (branch closures).
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 仕事といっても、月に2、3回（ ）ところです。
items.qr: Shigoto to itte mo, tsuki ni ni, san-kai (___) tokoro desu.
items.en: Even calling it "work," it's only about 2–3 times a month.
items.why: Day 6's 〜というところだ needs the という piece to form the rough-estimate pattern.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: このきゅうりは、（ ）味は抜群にいい。
items.qr: Kono kyuuri wa, (___) aji wa batsugun ni ii.
items.en: This cucumber's shape may be bad, but its taste is outstanding.

opts.en: the shape is admittedly bad, but

items.why: This is Day 1's plain Nこそ〜が concession — こそ marks the noun 形, and the adjective 悪い keeps its own plain form before が.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: この仕組みを（ ）無駄だよ。この会社は君が思う以上に保守的だから。
items.qr: Kono shikumi o (___) muda da yo. Kono kaisha wa kimi ga omou ijou ni hoshuteki dakara.
items.en: Even if you try to change this system, it's useless — this company is more conservative than you think.

opts.en: even if one tries to change

items.why: Day 6's としたって dismisses the attempt (trying to change the system) as futile.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 今時、こんな古い洗濯機を使っているのは、うち（ ）。
items.qr: Imadoki, konna furui sentakuki o tsukatte iru no wa, uchi (___).
items.en: These days, ours is about the only household still using such an old washing machine.

opts.t: ぐらいだとされている

items.why: Day 2's ぐらいのものだ limits the scope to exactly one household — "only ours."
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 高速料金の割引で、今度の連休は例年以上に渋滞する（ ）。
items.qr: Kousoku ryoukin no waribiki de, kondo no renkyuu wa reinen ijou ni juutai suru (___).
items.en: Because of the highway toll discount, this holiday is expected to be more congested than in past years.
items.why: Day 5's とみられる is the impersonal, evidence-based forecast — a traffic prediction, just like a news report.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 契約書は双方がそれぞれ保管する（ ）。
items.qr: Keiyakusho wa souhou ga sorezore hokan suru (___).
items.en: The contract shall be kept by both parties respectively.
items.why: Day 2's ものとする is the formal contract-clause pattern — exactly the register of this sentence.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 過去の失敗は過ぎたものとして（ ）。
items.qr: Kako no shippai wa sugita mono to shite (___).
items.en: It's better to treat past failures as things that are over and just forget them.

opts.t: どうしても覚えているものだ
opts.r: dou shite mo oboete iru mono da

opts.t: 思い出そうとしても思い出せない
思い出さずにはいられない
忘れてしまうほうがいい
opts.en: it's better to just forget it

items.why: "Treating failures as ものとして (a settled, past premise)" logically continues into "so it's best to forget them" — the other three options all involve still remembering, which contradicts treating it as over.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 寝ないでやったところで、（ ）。
items.qr: Nenaide yatta tokoro de, (___).
items.en: Even doing it without sleeping, it would probably be impossible to complete it.

opts.t: 疲れすぎて熟睡できないだろう
それを完成させるのは不可能だろう
opts.r: sore o kansei saseru no wa fukanou darou

opts.t: もう少し長く続けることができるだろう
opts.r: mou sukoshi nagaku tsuzukeru koto ga dekiru darou
opts.en: could continue a bit longer (positive, wrong tone)

opts.t: なんとかそれを仕上げることができるだろう
opts.r: nantoka sore o shiageru koto ga dekiru darou
opts.en: could somehow finish it (positive, wrong tone)

items.why: Day 6's 〜たところで…ない needs a negative continuation regardless of effort — only option 2 states a negative outcome; the other three are neutral or positive, which doesn't fit the pattern's built-in pessimism.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: …激しい稽古を積む（ ）、上に上がっていくことはできない。
items.why: Day 3's ことなしに — one cannot advance without accumulating intense training first.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: …十両格以上に上がれる者はわずか1割（ ）。

opts.t: ということにしている
opts.r: to iu koto ni shite iru

items.why: Day 6's といったところだ gives the rough figure — "only about 10%."
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: それでもこの関取（ ）、世間で一人前の力士として認められるのである。

opts.en: since it's typical of (wrong subject type)

items.why: Week 1 Day 1's 〜てこそ — recognition as a full-fledged wrestler only comes after becoming a sekitori, a necessary precondition.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 中には、そんな下働きや苦労を何年もする（ ）別の道を選んだほうがいいと…
items.why: Day 2's くらいなら — rather than years of menial hardship, some decide another path is preferable.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: …関取の地位を手にした力士には本当に（ ）。
items.why: Day 4's 〜させられる — the wrestlers' achievement is the external trigger that provokes involuntary admiration in the reader.
items.unit: Week 1 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼ったら、家に（ ）なり、パソコンの前に座るんだから……。
items.qr: Kare ttara, ie ni (___) nari, pasokon no mae ni suwaru n dakara...
items.en: Honestly, that guy — the moment he gets home, he sits down in front of the computer...

opts.en: past tense (wrong form before なり)

items.why: Point 3's なり ("as soon as") always takes the plain non-past verb form, never the past — 帰るなり, not 帰ったなり.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 私なりに

items.q: 私は素人だが、この詩を自分（ ）解釈してみた。
items.qr: Watashi wa shirouto da ga, kono shi o jibun (___) kaishaku shite mita.
items.en: I'm an amateur, but I tried interpreting this poem in my own way.
items.why: 自分なりに ("in my own way," scaled to one's own ability) is Point 2's fixed pattern; なりして isn't a recognized form.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 私なりに

items.q: 顔色が悪いですよ。（ ）、楽にしてください。
items.qr: Kaoiro ga warui desu yo. (___), raku ni shite kudasai.
items.en: You look pale. Please sit down or lie down (or whatever) and make yourself comfortable.

opts.t: 座るなり横になるなり
opts.r: suwaru nari yoko ni naru nari
opts.en: sit down or lie down (or whatever)

opts.t: 座りつつ横になりつつ
opts.en: (wrong pattern — can't sit and lie down simultaneously)

items.why: Point 1's なりなり offers two alternative actions to choose from; つつ (simultaneous action) makes no sense here since sitting and lying down can't happen at the same time.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 私なりに

items.q: 窓を開けた（ ）、変な虫が入ってきた。
items.qr: Mado o aketa (___), hen na mushi ga haitte kita.
items.en: The moment I opened the window, a strange bug came in.

opts.en: (wrong — なり needs the plain non-past 開ける, not 開けた)

items.why: The blank follows 開けた (plain past) — なり can only attach to the plain non-past form, so with a past-tense verb already given, とたん (which does take Vた) is the only grammatical option.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 私なりに

items.q: 最終電車に乗り遅れても、タクシーに（ ）して必ず家に帰ってきなさい。
items.qr: Saishuu densha ni noriokurete mo, takushii ni (___) shite kanarazu ie ni kaette kinasai.
items.en: Even if you miss the last train, take a taxi or walk (or whatever) but be sure to come home.

opts.t: 乗らないなら乗らないなり
opts.en: (wrong pattern — this is Point 2's なりに, doesn't fit listing options)

items.why: The sentence offers alternative ways to get home — exactly Point 1's なりなり; option b's なら〜なりに (Point 2) describes acting within a limitation, not listing alternatives.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 1 · 私なりに

items.q: 彼は、（ ）かまわず電話をかけてくる。
items.qr: Kare wa, (___) kamawazu denwa o kakete kuru.
items.en: He calls me regardless of whether it's morning or the middle of the night.

opts.t: 朝だろうが夜中だろうが
opts.r: asa darou ga yonaka darou ga

opts.en: (missing the が that makes this concessive)

items.why: Point 2's pattern needs が (or と) after each だろう to form the concessive "whether...or..."; without it, the two clauses don't connect grammatically.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · どんなに高かろうが

items.q: この部屋でどんなに（ ）、外からは何も聞こえません。
items.qr: Kono heya de donna ni (___), soto kara wa nani mo kikoemasen.
items.en: No matter how much noise you make in this room, nothing can be heard from outside.

opts.en: no matter how much one makes noise
(wrong pattern — であれ needs a noun/na-adj, not this verb form)

items.why: どんなに pairs with Point 3's volitional-concessive (騒ごうとも); であれ is Point 1's pattern, reserved for nouns/na-adjectives, not verbs like 騒ぐ.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · どんなに高かろうが

items.q: たとえ（ ）、明日の試合は予定どおり行います。
items.qr: Tatoe (___), ashita no shiai wa yotei doori okonaimasu.
items.en: Whether it rains or snows, tomorrow's match will proceed as scheduled.

opts.t: 雨であろうと雪であろうと
opts.r: ame de arou to yuki de arou to

opts.t: 雨が降るが雪が降るが
opts.r: ame ga furu ga yuki ga furu ga

items.why: たとえ ("even if") signals Point 2's volitional-concessive であろうと; plain-form ～が does not create a concessive meaning here.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · どんなに高かろうが

items.q: どの大学（ ）、進学先が決まってほっとした。
items.qr: Dono daigaku (___), shingakusaki ga kimatte hotto shita.
items.en: Whichever university it is, I felt relieved once my next school was decided.
items.why: どの大学であれ ("whichever university") is Point 1's だれ／どこ／何であれ family applied to どの大学; であると is just a plain conditional, not a concession.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · どんなに高かろうが

items.q: （ ）君の自由だが、他人に迷惑をかけることは許されない。
items.qr: (___) kimi no jiyuu da ga, tanin ni meiwaku o kakeru koto wa yurusarenai.
items.en: Whatever you do is your own business, but you're not allowed to inconvenience others.

opts.en: whatever it is (wrong — needs an action verb here)

items.why: The sentence is about an action ("do"), which needs 何をしようと (volitional of する); 何だろうが would describe a state/identity, not an action taken.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 2 · どんなに高かろうが

items.q: あなたが反対（ ）私は一人で行くつもりです。
items.qr: Anata ga hantai (___) watashi wa hitori de iku tsumori desu.
items.en: Whether you object or not, I intend to go alone.

opts.en: torn about whether to (wrong — no indecision here)

items.why: The speaker isn't undecided — they've already decided to go regardless; that's Point 2's とまいと ("whether or not, it doesn't affect my decision"), not Point 3's かまいか (genuine indecision).
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 行こうか行くまいか迷っている

items.q: 大学院へ（ ）悩んだ末、いい仕事が見つかったので就職することにした。
items.qr: Daigakuin e (___) nayanda sue, ii shigoto ga mitsukatta node shuushoku suru koto ni shita.
items.en: After agonizing over whether to go to graduate school or not, I found a good job and decided to start working instead.

opts.en: whether one goes or not (wrong — no indecision word here)

items.why: 悩んだ ("agonized") is the tell — this describes real indecision, exactly Point 3's かまいか, not Point 2's とまいと (which describes indifference to an outcome, not indecision).
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 行こうか行くまいか迷っている

items.q: 来週の会合に（ ）、必ず資料に目を通してください。
items.qr: Raishuu no kaigou ni (___), kanarazu shiryou ni me o tooshite kudasai.
items.en: Whether you come to next week's meeting or not, please be sure to go through the materials.

opts.t: 来るにしろ来ないにしろ
opts.r: kuru ni shiro konai ni shiro

opts.t: 来るというか来ないというか
opts.r: kuru to iu ka konai to iu ka
opts.en: hard to say whether coming or not (wrong — describes description, not concession)

items.why: The instruction ("go through the materials regardless") needs Point 4's にしろ concession; というか is only for hedging a description, not for saying an outcome is unaffected.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 行こうか行くまいか迷っている

items.q: 欠席（ ）連絡はしてください。
items.qr: Kesseki (___) renraku wa shite kudasai.
items.en: Even if you're going to be absent, please let us know.

opts.en: (wrong conjugation — にしろ takes plain form, not volitional)

items.why: にせよ／にしろ attach to the plain form (欠席する), not the volitional (欠席しよう) — するにせよ is correct, しようにしろ is not a valid combination.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 行こうか行くまいか迷っている

items.q: それは、（ ）、とにかく変わったものだ。
items.qr: Sore wa, (___), tonikaku kawatta mono da.
items.en: That's — how should I put it — interesting, or maybe unusual, but in any case, it's a strange thing.

opts.t: 面白かろうと、珍しかろうと
opts.en: whether interesting or unusual (wrong — this concedes, doesn't describe)

opts.t: 面白いというか、珍しいというか
opts.r: omoshiroi to iu ka, mezurashii to iu ka
opts.en: you could call it interesting, or unusual

items.why: The speaker is hedging on how to describe something (とにかく変わったものだ, "anyway, it's a strange thing") — exactly Point 1's というか, not a concessive volitional form.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 3 · 行こうか行くまいか迷っている

items.q: 彼女はまだ若いけれど、（ ）申し分のない女性だ。
items.qr: Kanojo wa mada wakai keredo, (___) moushibun no nai josei da.
items.en: She's still young, but she's a flawless woman in terms of both experience and ability.

opts.t: 経験といい能力といい
opts.r: keiken to ii nouryoku to ii
keiken da no nouryoku da no
opts.en: experience, ability, whatever (wrong tone — this is a compliment, not a complaint)

items.why: 申し分のない ("flawless") is praise, matching Point 2's neutral-to-positive といい; だのだの (Point 1) is reserved for a complaining tone, which contradicts praising her.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 4 · デザインといい、色といい

items.q: 猫に（ ）引っかかれてしまった。
items.qr: Neko ni (___) hikkakarete shimatta.
items.en: I got scratched by the cat — not just on the face, but on my hands too (everywhere).

opts.en: face or hand or whatever (wrong — implies choice, not universal coverage)

opts.t: 顔といわず手といわず
opts.r: kao to iwazu te to iwazu
opts.en: not just the face, but the hands too — everywhere

items.why: Being scratched "everywhere" is Point 4's といわず (universal extent); なりなり (Week 2 Day 1's pattern) suggests a choice between options, which doesn't fit "scratched all over."
items.unit: Week 2 Day 4 · デザインといい、色といい

items.q: こんなつまらない商品を、売るほうも売るほう（ ）買うほうも買うほうだ。
items.qr: Konna tsumaranai shouhin o, uru hou mo uru hou (___) kau hou mo kau hou da.
items.en: Whoever's selling such a worthless product is bad enough, and whoever's buying it is just as bad.
items.why: 売るほうも売るほうなら、買うほうも買うほうだ is exactly Point 3's shared-blame construction; だろうが would turn it into an unrelated concessive.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 4 · デザインといい、色といい

items.q: 彼は、（ ）何かしら口に入れている。
items.qr: Kare wa, (___) nanikashira kuchi ni irete iru.
items.en: He always has something in his mouth — gum, candy, or whatever.

opts.r: gamu da no ame da no

opts.en: gum or candy (wrong — implies a choice, not an observed habit)

items.why: This describes his habitual behavior (always has something), matching Point 1's だのだの list of examples; なりなり would suggest he's choosing between options, not habitually doing both.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 4 · デザインといい、色といい

items.q: A「あの人、田中さんのお母さんだよね。派手だね。」B「（ ）。」
items.qr: A: "Ano hito, Tanaka-san no okaasan da yo ne. Hade da ne." B: "(___)."
items.en: A: "That's Tanaka-san's mother, right? She's flashy." B: "Well, if the daughter's like that, the mother's just as bad."

opts.t: 娘が娘なら母親も母親だね
opts.r: musume ga musume nara haha oya mo haha oya da ne
opts.en: if the daughter's like that, so is the mother

opts.t: 娘といい母親といい親子なんだね
opts.r: musume to ii haha oya to ii oyako nan da ne
opts.en: (too neutral — mismatches the critical tone of "flashy")

items.why: "She's flashy" is a mild criticism; Point 3's N1もN1なら shares that critical tone (blaming mother and daughter together), while といい is tone-neutral and doesn't carry the implied criticism.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 4 · デザインといい、色といい

items.q: 今朝から雪が（ ）を繰り返している。
items.qr: Kesa kara yuki ga (___) o kurikaeshite iru.
items.en: Since this morning, the snow has repeatedly started and stopped, over and over.

opts.t: 降るならやみ、降るならやみ
opts.r: furu nara yami, furu nara yami

opts.t: 降ってはやみ、降ってはやみ
opts.r: futte wa yami, futte wa yami
opts.en: starts and stops, over and over

items.why: A repeated cycle (snow starting, then stopping, again and again) is exactly Point 3's てはVて repeated twice; ならやみ isn't a recognized grammatical combination.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 5 · 行きつ戻りつ

items.q: 彼と私は、学生時代、（ ）成績を争ったものだ。
items.qr: Kare to watashi wa, gakusei jidai, (___) seiseki o arasotta mono da.
items.en: Back in our school days, he and I used to compete for grades, trading the lead back and forth.

opts.t: 抜こうが抜かれまいが
opts.en: whether overtaking or not (wrong — no such indifference here)

items.why: Competing neck-and-neck for grades is Point 4's つ〜つ back-and-forth pattern; the volitional-concessive がまいが (Week 2 Day 3's pattern) would describe indifference to an outcome, not an actual seesawing competition.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 5 · 行きつ戻りつ

items.q: 若いころは、お酒を（ ）踊ったものだ。
items.qr: Wakai koro wa, osake o (___) odotta mono da.
items.en: Back when I was young, I used to drink and dance, over and over.

opts.en: trying to drink (wrong — describes an attempt, not a habitual repeated act)

items.why: A habitual "drink then dance" cycle from one's youth is Point 2's repeated ては; 飲もうとして describes merely attempting to drink, not a completed, repeated habit.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 5 · 行きつ戻りつ

items.q: 学んだことを（ ）を繰り返している。
items.qr: Mananda koto o (___) o kurikaeshite iru.
items.en: I keep learning and then forgetting what I've learned, over and over.

opts.t: 覚えるし忘れ、覚えるし忘れ
opts.r: oboeru shi wasure, oboeru shi wasure

opts.t: 覚えては忘れ、覚えては忘れ
opts.r: oboete wa wasure, oboete wa wasure
opts.en: learn and forget, over and over

items.why: The repeated two-step cycle (learn, then forget) is Point 3's てはVて said twice; し (a plain "and" connector) doesn't create this repeated-cycle meaning.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 5 · 行きつ戻りつ

items.q: 遅刻したと言っても、電車の事故（ ）仕方がない。
items.qr: Chikoku shita to itte mo, densha no jiko (___) shikata ga nai.
items.en: Even though you were late, if it was because of a train accident, it can't be helped.

opts.en: (wrong — this is an unrelated fixed phrase meaning "uniquely characteristic of")

items.why: Point 1's では is the simple conditional ("if it's a train accident, it can't be helped"); ならでは is a completely different fixed expression meaning "something only possible because of X" (e.g. 日本ならではの文化).
items.unit: Week 2 Day 5 · 行きつ戻りつ

items.q: 仕事がないので毎日友達と遊んでいる。（ ）。
items.qr: Shigoto ga nai node mainichi tomodachi to asonde iru. (___).
items.en: I have no job so I hang out with friends every day. I honestly can't tell if I'm idle or busy.

opts.t: 暇なのやら忙しいのやら
opts.r: hima na no yara isogashii no yara
opts.en: can't tell if idle or busy

opts.r: hima to mo isogashii to mo
opts.en: (grammatically close, but のやら's wondering tone fits the self-deprecating joke better here)

items.why: The speaker is being wryly self-deprecating about a day filled with "nothing to do" that nonetheless feels busy with friends — Point 3's のやら captures that half-joking, torn-between-two-readings tone that plain とも doesn't quite carry.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 6 · いつまで続くのやら

items.q: ペットは（ ）大変だけれど、ペットのいない生活は考えられない。
items.qr: Petto wa (___) taihen dakeredo, petto no inai seikatsu wa kangaerarenai.
items.en: Pets come with their own hassles, but I can't imagine life without one.

opts.t: いるともいないとも言えなくて
opts.r: iru to mo inai to mo ienakute
opts.en: can't say whether there is one or not (wrong — doesn't fit; pets clearly exist here)
if you have one, that comes with its own issue

items.why: Having a pet brings its own (minor) hassle, yet is still worthwhile — exactly Point 2's たらたで; とも is for judgment between two possibilities, which doesn't fit since having a pet is a given fact here.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 6 · いつまで続くのやら

items.q: 会社が倒産しそうだ。（ ）ことやら……。
items.qr: Kaisha ga tousan shisou da. (___) koto yara...
items.en: The company looks like it might go bankrupt. I have no idea what will happen...
items.why: Wondering about an uncertain future outcome needs どう ("how/what") + なる, matching Point 4's exasperated wondering; 何する doesn't fit this context grammatically or semantically.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 6 · いつまで続くのやら

items.q: 彼は（ ）言えるが、とにかく口数が少ない。
items.qr: Kare wa (___) ieru ga, tonikaku kuchikazu ga sukunai.
items.en: You could call him quiet, or you could call him passive, but in any case, he doesn't talk much.

opts.t: おとなしいとも消極的だとも
opts.r: otonashii to mo shoukyokuteki da to mo
opts.en: could call him quiet or passive

opts.t: おとなしいのやら消極的なのやらと
opts.r: otonashii no yara shoukyokuteki na no yara to
opts.en: (wrong — おとなしい and 消極的 aren't opposites, so のやら doesn't fit)

items.why: Point 1's とも simply offers two possible descriptions without requiring them to be opposites; Point 3's のやら specifically requires an opposite pair (◆aとbは反対の意味), and quiet/passive aren't opposites — they're actually quite similar.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 6 · いつまで続くのやら

items.q: （ ）、はっきり言ってください。
items.qr: (___), hakkiri itte kudasai.
items.en: If you don't want to, just say so clearly.

opts.en: if you don't want to, that's fine too, but (say so)

opts.t: いやともいやじゃないとも
opts.r: iya to mo iya ja nai to mo
opts.en: (wrong — doesn't fit the imperative "just tell me clearly")

items.why: "If X, then X — but say so clearly" is Point 2's たらたで pattern (accepting either outcome, just wanting clarity); とも is about the speaker's own inability to judge, not a request for someone else to clarify their stance.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 6 · いつまで続くのやら

items.q: 飲食店は、（ ）の良さがあると思う。
items.qr: Inshokuten wa, (___) no yosa ga aru to omou.
items.en: I think restaurants have their own kind of merit — a small one has the merits appropriate to being small.

opts.t: 小さいだの大きいだの
opts.r: chiisai da no ookii da no
opts.en: small, big, whatever (wrong tone — complaining, not appreciating)

opts.t: 小さいのやら大きいのやら
opts.r: chiisai no yara ookii no yara
opts.en: can't tell if small or big (wrong — not about uncertainty)

opts.t: 小さいなら小さいなり
opts.en: small has its own appropriate merits

items.why: Week 2 Day 1's なら〜なりに praises something as appropriately fitting to its own scale — exactly the sentiment here.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: その映画は、警官と犯人が（ ）の展開ではらはらするものだった。
items.qr: Sono eiga wa, keikan to hannin ga (___) no tenkai de harahara suru mono datta.
items.en: That movie had a thrilling back-and-forth development between the police officer and the criminal.

opts.en: chasing and being chased (plausible, but less precise than option 3 for a police thriller)
alternately getting ahead and falling behind

items.why: Week 2 Day 5's つ〜つ back-and-forth pattern fits a tense thriller where the lead keeps swapping between the two sides.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: （ ）、顧客にこの件を説明すべきだった。
items.qr: (___), kokyaku ni kono ken o setsumei subeki datta.
items.en: Whether it's the president or an employee, someone should have explained this matter to the client.

opts.r: shachou da no shain da no
opts.en: president, employee, whatever (wrong — complaining tone doesn't fit)

opts.t: 社長となり社員となり
opts.r: shachou to nari shain to nari
shachou to mo shain to mo
opts.en: can't say president or employee (wrong — not about uncertain judgment)

opts.t: 社長であれ社員であれ
opts.r: shachou de are shain de are

items.why: Week 2 Day 2's であれであれ concedes that the rule (someone should explain) applies regardless of rank.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: この旅館は、窓からの眺め（ ）料理（ ）、申し分がない。
items.qr: Kono ryokan wa, mado kara no nagame (___) ryouri (___), moushibun ga nai.
items.en: This inn is flawless both in terms of the view from the window and the food.

opts.en: or whatever (wrong — this praises both, not offers a choice)
can't tell (wrong — not an opposite pair, not uncertain)

items.why: Two positive aspects supporting one overall praise (申し分がない, "flawless") is exactly Week 2 Day 4's といいといい.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 隣の公園で遊ぶ子どもの声がうるさくて仕方がないが、どこに苦情を（ ）わからない。
items.qr: Tonari no kouen de asobu kodomo no koe ga urusakute shikata ga nai ga, doko ni kujou o (___) wakaranai.
items.en: The noise of children playing in the park next door is unbearable, but I have no idea where to even direct a complaint.

opts.en: if one were to dare say it (wrong pattern)
whether it's okay to say — no idea
even if one says it (wrong — doesn't fit わからない)
whether one says it or not (wrong — no indifference implied)

items.why: Week 2 Day 6's ものやら fits the open-ended "I don't know" wondering (paired with わからない) about where to even begin complaining.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 両親が（ ）高校をやめて働くつもりだ。
items.qr: Ryoushin ga (___) koukou o yamete hataraku tsumori da.
items.en: No matter what my parents say, I intend to quit high school and go to work.

opts.en: whatever they say (plausible, but doesn't fit the given verb pattern as cleanly as option 3)

opts.r: nani o iou to shite mo
opts.en: no matter what they try to say
(wrong — this describes indecision, not the parents' words)

items.why: "No matter what they say/try to say" needs a volitional + としても concessive; option 3 matches this most directly and naturally in modern speech.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼が金持ち（ ）私には関係ありません。
items.qr: Kare ga kanemochi (___) watashi ni wa kankei arimasen.
items.en: Whether he is rich or not is none of my concern.

opts.t: だろうがないだろうが
opts.en: (wrong — ない doesn't pair correctly with だろう here)

opts.r: de aru to ja nai to

opts.t: だろうとないだろうと
であろうとなかろうと

items.why: Week 2 Day 2's fixed であろうとなかろうと ("whether or not") is the correctly-formed affirmative/negative volitional pair.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: ここは不便でどの駅に（ ）、徒歩で20分以上かかる。
items.qr: Koko wa fuben de dono eki ni (___), toho de nijuppun ijou kakaru.
items.en: This place is inconvenient — whichever station you go to, it takes more than 20 minutes on foot.

opts.en: whichever one goes to, in any case
(wrong — needs a paired volitional, and doesn't fit どの駅に)

items.why: どの駅に (a question-word-like phrase) + にせよ is Week 2 Day 3's fixed "in any case" family, just like 何にせよ／だれにせよ.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: レポートを（ ）しているので、1時間たってもまだ1枚もできない。
items.qr: Repooto o (___) shite iru node, ichijikan tatte mo mada ichi-mai mo dekinai.
items.en: I keep writing and erasing the report, so even after an hour I haven't completed a single page.

opts.t: 書くなり消し書くなり消し
opts.r: kaku nari keshi kaku nari keshi

opts.t: 書いたが消し書いたが消し
opts.r: kaita ga keshi kaita ga keshi

opts.t: 書くなら消し書くなら消し
opts.r: kaku nara keshi kaku nara keshi

opts.t: 書いては消し書いては消し
opts.r: kaite wa keshi kaite wa keshi
opts.en: write and erase, over and over

items.why: A repeated two-step cycle (write, then erase) matching Week 2 Day 5's てはVて said twice.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: この魚は生では食べられないから、煮る（ ）焼く（ ）してください。
items.qr: Kono sakana wa nama de wa taberarenai kara, niru (___) yaku (___) shite kudasai.
items.en: This fish can't be eaten raw, so please either boil it or grill it (or whatever).

opts.en: both ~ and ~ (wrong — not offering a choice of cooking method)

items.why: Week 2 Day 1's なりなり offers a couple of acceptable cooking methods — either works.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼女は立派な家に住んでいるのに、掃除が大変（ ）キッチンが使いにくい（ ）と文句ばかり言っている。
items.qr: Kanojo wa rippa na ie ni sunde iru noni, souji ga taihen (___) kicchin ga tsukainikui (___) to monku bakari itte iru.
items.en: Even though she lives in a fine house, all she does is complain that cleaning is a hassle, the kitchen is hard to use, and so on.

opts.en: (wrong tone — offers a choice, not complaints)

opts.r: na no yara / na no yara
opts.en: (wrong — not an opposite pair, not uncertainty)

items.why: 文句ばかり言っている ("does nothing but complain") is the clear signal for Week 2 Day 4's だのだの.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 息子の部屋は、壁（ ）天井（ ）、サッカーのポスターだらけである。
items.qr: Musuko no heya wa, kabe (___) tenjou (___), sakkaa no posutaa darake de aru.
items.en: My son's room is plastered with soccer posters — not just the walls, but the ceiling too.

opts.t: といおうか／といおうか
opts.r: to iou ka / to iou ka

opts.t: ともいおうか／ともいおうか
opts.r: to mo iou ka / to mo iou ka

opts.t: ともいわず／ともいわず
opts.r: to mo iwazu / to mo iwazu

items.why: "Covered everywhere, not just the walls" is exactly Week 2 Day 4's といわずといわず extending beyond the two named surfaces.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 家の壁紙を張り替えようと思う。自分でやる（ ）人に頼む（ ）、大変だ。
items.qr: Ie no kabegami o harikaeyou to omou. Jibun de yaru (___) hito ni tanomu (___), taihen da.
items.en: I'm thinking of re-papering the walls at home. Whether I do it myself or ask someone to do it, it's a hassle either way.

opts.r: to iu ka / to iu ka
opts.en: you could call it, or (wrong — this is about description, not two courses of action)
(wrong — not about extending beyond named categories)
whether ~ or ~, either way it's a hassle
(wrong — needs a matching volitional, doesn't fit plain form here)

items.why: Two different courses of action (do it yourself, or hire someone) both leading to the same conclusion (a hassle) is exactly Week 2 Day 3's にせよにせよ.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 自分の子どもが問題を起こして学校に呼び出されているのに、それを無視する親がいる。（ ）。
items.qr: Jibun no kodomo ga mondai o okoshite gakkou ni yobidasarete iru noni, sore o mushi suru oya ga iru. (___).
items.en: There are parents who ignore being called to school even though their child caused trouble. If the child is like that, the parent is just as bad.

opts.t: 子どもといわず親といわずだ
opts.r: kodomo to iwazu oya to iwazu da
opts.en: (wrong — this is for universal extent, not shared blame)

opts.t: 子どもが子どもなら親も親だ
opts.r: kodomo ga kodomo nara oya mo oya da
opts.en: if the child is like that, so is the parent

opts.t: 子どもといい親といいだ
opts.r: kodomo to ii oya to ii da
opts.en: (wrong grammatically — といい can't end a sentence with だ like this)

opts.t: 子どもだろうか親だろうかだ
opts.r: kodomo darou ka oya darou ka da

items.why: Blaming the child and the parent together for the same underlying fault is exactly Week 2 Day 4's N1もN1なら、N2もN2だ.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 客が来ようが来まいが、（ ）。
items.qr: Kyaku ga koyou ga komai ga, (___).
items.en: Whether customers come or not, I have to open the shop.

opts.t: 料理を作るとも言えない
opts.r: ryouri o tsukuru to mo ienai

opts.t: 料理を作ってもむだになるだろう
opts.r: ryouri o tsukutte mo muda ni naru darou
opts.en: (plausible but narrower — about food waste specifically, not the shop's operation)

opts.t: 店を開けなければならない
店を開けようかと悩む
opts.r: mise o akeyou ka to nayamu
opts.en: torn about whether to open (contradicts the "doesn't matter" concession)

items.why: Having already conceded indifference to whether customers show up (来ようが来まいが), the natural continuation is a firm, unaffected obligation — opening the shop regardless — not renewed indecision (option 4 would contradict the concession already made).
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 葬式に（ ）迷ったが…

opts.t: 出席しようかするまいか
出席しようがしまいが
opts.en: whether attending or not, indifferent (wrong — contradicts 迷ったが)

opts.t: 出席しようとなかろうと
出席しようともなかろうとも

items.why: 迷ったが ("was torn, but") explicitly signals real indecision — Week 2 Day 3's ようかまいか.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 電話（22-a）メール（22-b）して、彼を励まそうかとも思ったが…

opts.t: aするなり／bするなりして
opts.r: a suru nari / b suru nari shite

opts.t: aするであれ／bするであれ
opts.r: a suru de are / b suru de are
opts.en: (wrong — であれ needs nouns/na-adj, not verbs)

opts.t: aしようというか／bしようというか
opts.r: a shiyou to iu ka / b shiyou to iu ka
opts.en: (wrong — というか hedges a description, not an action choice)

opts.t: aであろうと／bであろうとして
opts.r: a de arou to / b de arou to shite

items.why: Week 2 Day 1's なりなりして offers two loosely equivalent methods (call or email) for reaching out.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼も何も言わずに自分の机に向かったが、席に（ ）「田中さんって、優しいですね。」…

opts.en: (wrong — なり needs the plain non-past, not the te-form)
(wrong — なり needs the plain non-past, not the past form)
(wrong pattern entirely — this is the "in one's own way" なりに)

items.why: Week 2 Day 1's "as soon as" なり always takes the plain non-past verb — 着くなり, matching how he murmured the line the instant he reached his seat.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼の気持ちを考えるとかわいそう（24-a）悲しい（24-b）、なんとも言えない気持ちで…

opts.r: a da to ii / b to ii
opts.en: (wrong — といい supports one conclusion, doesn't fit "indescribable" mix)

opts.r: a darou ka / b darou ka
a to iwazu / b to iwazu
opts.en: (wrong — といわず is for universal extent, not mixed description)

opts.r: a to iu ka / b to iu ka
opts.en: you could call it pitiable, or sad

items.why: "An indescribable feeling" (なんとも言えない気持ち) is the classic setup for Week 2 Day 3's というかというか, hedging between two hard-to-separate emotions.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼のいない机を見ては心を痛めているだけの自分だったが、（ ）、まず自分の気持ちを伝えるべきだった…

opts.en: anyway, in any case (variant of 何はともあれ)
whatever it is (wrong — this concedes identity, not "anyway")

items.why: 何ともあれ is a variant of the fixed idiom 何はともあれ ("anyway, first and foremost") — pivoting from dwelling on the empty desk to what should have been done instead.
items.unit: Week 2 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 来たくなければ来なくてもいい。ただ君が損を（ ）までだ。
items.qr: Kitakunakereba konakute mo ii. Tada kimi ga son o (___) made da.
items.en: You don't have to come if you don't want to. It's just that you'll be the one who loses out, nothing more.

opts.en: plain non-past (correct form before までだ)

items.why: Point 1's まで（のこと）だ needs 損をする ("to lose out"), stating that's simply the consequence — 損をしない would reverse the meaning entirely.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 毎日はしないまでも

items.q: 親が出る（ ）、子どもたちだけでその問題を解決した。
items.qr: Oya ga deru (___), kodomotachi dake de sono mondai o kaiketsu shita.
items.en: Without even needing the parents to step in, the kids solved the problem themselves.
items.why: Point 4's までもない (here in its て-form, までもなく, linking into the next clause) — the kids didn't even need their parents to intervene.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 毎日はしないまでも

items.q: あの人とは話はしない（ ）、挨拶ぐらいはしますよ。
items.qr: Ano hito to wa hanashi wa shinai (___), aisatsu gurai wa shimasu yo.
items.en: Even if I don't talk with that person, I at least say hello.

opts.en: without even needing to (wrong — doesn't lower a bar)

items.why: Point 2's ないまでも sets a modest minimum (a greeting) after conceding the fuller action (talking) won't happen.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 毎日はしないまでも

items.q: いくらお金を稼いでも死んでしまえば（ ）。
items.qr: Ikura okane o kaseide mo shinde shimaeba (___).
items.en: No matter how much money you earn, once you die, that's the end of it.

opts.en: (not a valid combination of these two patterns)

items.why: それまでだ is the fixed idiom for "that's it, nothing more can be done" — それまでもない mixes two unrelated patterns and isn't a real form.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 毎日はしないまでも

items.q: これくらいの故障、修理を頼む（ ）。僕が直してあげるよ。
items.qr: Kore kurai no koshou, shuuri o tanomu (___). Boku ga naoshite ageru yo.
items.en: For a malfunction this minor, there's no need to even call for a repair. I'll fix it for you.

opts.en: (wrong — this downplays an action already taken, not dismisses a future need)

items.why: A minor malfunction not warranting a repair call is Point 4's までもない; までのことだ describes something already done as trivial, not something not yet needed.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 1 · 毎日はしないまでも

items.q: 応援していたチームが試合に負けてしまって残念（ ）。
items.qr: Ouen shite ita chiimu ga shiai ni makete shimatte zannen (___).
items.en: I'm so disappointed that the team I was cheering for lost the match.

opts.en: is the best (wrong — not a recommendation here)

items.why: 残念な限りだ intensifies the emotion (disappointment) to its peak — Point 1; に限る is for recommending a best option, unrelated to expressing feelings.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 今日を限りに

items.q: 新築の家を買った。今月（ ）このマンションともお別れだ。
items.qr: Shinchiku no ie o katta. Kongetsu (___) kono manshon tomo owakare da.
items.en: I bought a newly-built house. As of this month, I'll be saying goodbye to this apartment too.

opts.en: (wrong — this means "restricted to," an unrelated pattern)

items.why: Point 2's を限りに marks "this month" as the definite ending point of living in the apartment; に限り (note: different from 限りで) means "restricted only to," a different, unrelated meaning.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 今日を限りに

items.q: 風邪をひいたときは、薬など飲むよりゆっくり寝る（ ）。
items.qr: Kaze o hiita toki wa, kusuri nado nomu yori yukkuri neru (___).
items.en: When you catch a cold, sleeping well is better than taking medicine — nothing beats it.

opts.en: nothing beats it, is the best
(wrong — 限りだ needs an emotional adjective, not a verb)

items.why: This is a recommendation ("sleeping is best") — Point 3's に限る; 限りだ attaches to emotional adjectives (Point 1), not to a verb like 寝る here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 今日を限りに

items.q: 朝の電車が混んでいるのは、今日に（ ）ことではない。
items.qr: Asa no densha ga konde iru no wa, kyou ni (___) koto de wa nai.
items.en: The morning train being crowded isn't limited to today.

opts.en: (wrong form — needs the plain past 限った before ことではない)

items.why: Point 4's に限ったことではない always uses the plain-past 限った before ことではない, not the plain non-past 限る.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 今日を限りに

items.q: 宝くじに当たったなんて、なんともうらやましい（ ）。
items.qr: Takarakuji ni atatta nante, nantomo urayamashii (___).
items.en: Winning the lottery — how incredibly enviable!

opts.en: not limited to (wrong — no such claim here)

items.why: うらやましい限りだ intensifies envy to its peak — exactly Point 1's job.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 2 · 今日を限りに

items.q: 近所の人の話では、昨夜あの家でだれかが亡くなった（ ）。
items.qr: Kinjo no hito no hanashi de wa, sakuya ano ie de dareka ga naku natta (___).
items.en: According to a neighbor, someone in that house passed away last night.

opts.en: (not a valid combination — らしい already implies hearsay, redundant with という)

items.why: Relaying a neighbor's secondhand report needs Point 4's とのことだ; というらしい double-stacks two hearsay markers incorrectly.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 兄弟といえども

items.q: 入社したばかり（ ）、もう少しまともな挨拶ができないのだろうか。
items.qr: Nyuusha shita bakari (___), mou sukoshi matomo na aisatsu ga dekinai no darou ka.
items.en: Even though he just joined the company, couldn't he manage a slightly more proper greeting?
items.why: Conceding he's new while still expecting basic manners is Point 2's とはいえ; とは alone would express surprise, not a concession leading to a criticism.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 兄弟といえども

items.q: 親（ ）、子どもをしかるのに暴力はいけない。
items.qr: Oya (___), kodomo o shikaru no ni bouryoku wa ikenai.
items.en: Even parents shouldn't use violence to scold their children.
items.why: A strong, formal moral assertion ("even parents shouldn't...") calls for Point 3's といえども; に限り is Day 2's "restricted to" pattern, unrelated here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 兄弟といえども

items.q: 鈴木さんから、今日は風邪で休む（ ）電話がありました。
items.qr: Suzuki-san kara, kyou wa kaze de yasumu (___) denwa ga arimashita.
items.en: Suzuki-san called to say he'll be off today with a cold.

opts.en: a call that... (attaches to a noun, 電話)

items.why: との directly modifies the noun 電話 ("a call that...") — Point 4's [文]とのN; とはいう isn't a grammatical construction.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 兄弟といえども

items.q: あんなに女らしく美しく見える人が、実は男だった（ ）……。
items.qr: Anna ni onna rashiku utsukushiku mieru hito ga, jitsu wa otoko datta (___)...
items.en: Someone who looks so feminine and beautiful actually being a man — what a surprise...
items.why: The trailing "……" after a shocking revelation is the classic Point 1 とは exclamation of surprise; とはいえ would need a following clause that concedes and continues, not just trails off in shock.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 3 · 兄弟といえども

items.q: あの先生は僕が何を尋ねても、いつも誠意（ ）答えてくれる。
items.qr: Ano sensei wa boku ga nani o tazunete mo, itsumo seii (___) kotaete kureru.
items.en: Whatever I ask that teacher, they always answer sincerely.

opts.en: (too formal — an over-elevated register for everyday teacher-student description)

items.why: 誠意をもって ("with sincerity," Point 2①) describes a manner/means of answering; もちまして is the extra-humble variant reserved for formal ceremony/announcement contexts, mismatched here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 努力をもって

items.q: 私の父は定年退職（ ）、一日中テレビばかり見ている。
items.qr: Watashi no chichi wa teinen taishoku (___), ichinichijuu terebi bakari mite iru.
items.en: Ever since my father retired, all he does all day is watch TV.

opts.en: starting with (wrong — retirement doesn't "expand," it's a single continuous state after)

items.why: A continuous unbroken habit since retirement is Point 3's てからというもの; を皮切りに is for a starting point that then expands into a growing series, which doesn't fit "watching TV all day" as a static continuous state.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 努力をもって

items.q: 当選者の発表は、商品の発送（ ）代えさせていただきます。
items.qr: Tousensha no happyou wa, shouhin no hassou (___) kaesasete itadakimasu.
items.en: The announcement of winners will be replaced by the shipping of the product (i.e., only winners will receive a shipment; that itself serves as notification).

opts.en: by means of (product shipment serves as the notification)
starting with (wrong — no expanding series here)

items.why: This is Point 2①'s "means" sense — shipping the product itself substitutes for a formal announcement; を皮切りに would need a growing series of events, not a one-time substitution.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 努力をもって

items.q: 一人暮らしを始めてから（ ）、まともな食事をしたことがない。
items.qr: Hitorigurashi o hajimete kara (___), matomo na shokuji o shita koto ga nai.
items.en: Ever since I started living alone, I haven't had a single proper meal.

opts.en: even ~ (wrong — a concession, not a duration marker)

items.why: A continuous state since a starting point is Point 3's てからというもの; といえども (Day 3's pattern) is an unrelated concession.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 努力をもって

items.q: 昨日の会議では、彼の発言（ ）反対意見が次々と出た。
items.qr: Kinou no kaigi de wa, kare no hatsugen (___) hantai iken ga tsugitsugi to deta.
items.en: At yesterday's meeting, starting with his remark, objections came pouring in one after another.

opts.en: starting with (and then a series follows)
ever since (wrong — this is a single event triggering a series, not a continuous duration)

items.why: One remark triggering a growing series of objections is exactly Point 1's を皮切りに; というもの describes an unbroken continuous state, not a triggering event.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 4 · 努力をもって

items.q: あの人はいつも電車に乗り込む（ ）、席を確保しようとする。
items.qr: Ano hito wa itsumo densha ni norikomu (___), seki o kakuho shiyou to suru.
items.en: That person always tries to grab a seat the instant they board the train.

opts.en: once ~, inevitably (wrong — no unstoppable chain reaction here)

items.why: Boarding immediately followed by grabbing a seat is a simple instant-timing pattern — Point 2's が早いか; が最後 requires an unstoppable ongoing consequence (like playing games all night), not a quick one-off reaction.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 休めるかと思いきや

items.q: 彼女は家に（ ）や、いきなりトイレに駆け込んだ。
items.qr: Kanojo wa ie ni (___) ya, ikinari toire ni kakekonda.
items.en: The moment she entered the house, she rushed straight to the bathroom.

opts.en: (wrong — や needs the plain non-past, not the past)

items.why: Point 1's や（否や） always attaches to the plain non-past verb form, exactly like なり from Week 2 Day 1.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 休めるかと思いきや

items.q: やっと富士山の頂上に着いた（ ）、まだ8合目だった。
items.qr: Yatto Fujisan no choujou ni tsuita (___), mada hachigou-me datta.
items.en: I thought I'd finally reached the summit of Mt. Fuji, but it turned out I was only at the 8th station.

opts.en: thought that..., but contrary to expectations
the instant (wrong — no second immediate action, just a reversed expectation)

items.why: A mistaken expectation (thought summit, was actually only 8th station) is Point 4's と思いきや; が早いか needs a fast follow-up action, not a corrected belief.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 休めるかと思いきや

items.q: 119番の通報を受ける（ ）、救急車は出動した。
items.qr: Hyaku-juu-kyuu-ban no tsuuhou o ukeru (___), kyuukyuusha wa shutsudou shita.
items.en: No sooner had the emergency call come in than the ambulance was dispatched.

opts.en: once ~, inevitably (wrong — no ongoing unstoppable chain)

items.why: A single quick reaction (dispatch) following a trigger (the call) is Point 2's が早いか; が最後 is for an ongoing, unstoppable habit, not a one-time emergency response.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 休めるかと思いきや

items.q: 彼は普段はとてもおとなしいが、ひとたび（ ）暴れて手がつけられなくなる。
items.qr: Kare wa fudan wa totemo otonashii ga, hitotabi (___) abarete te ga tsukerarenaku naru.
items.en: He's usually very calm, but once he gets angry, there's no stopping him — he goes wild.

opts.en: the instant he gets angry (wrong — misses the ongoing unstoppable consequence)

items.why: ひとたび ("once") pairs with Point 3's たら最後 — describing a character trait where anger triggers an unstoppable rampage, not just a quick reaction.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 5 · 休めるかと思いきや

items.q: 食べる（ ）次の料理がどんどん運ばれて、ゆっくり味わえなかった。
items.qr: Taberu (___) tsugi no ryouri ga dondon hakobarete, yukkuri ajiwaenakatta.
items.en: The next dish kept arriving the moment I finished eating, so I couldn't savor anything slowly.

opts.en: while also (wrong — this isn't two ongoing life-roles)

items.why: Dishes arriving the instant one finishes eating each course is Point 1's そばから; かたわら describes two parallel ongoing occupations, not a rapid-fire dining sequence.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 散歩がてら

items.q: 今日は先日のご報告（ ）、部下の紹介に参りました。
items.qr: Kyou wa senjitsu no go-houkoku (___), buka no shoukai ni mairimashita.
items.en: Today I've come both to report on the other day's matter and to introduce my subordinate.

opts.en: while also (wrong — no two ongoing roles here)

items.why: A formal visit combining a report with an introduction is Point 4's かたがた; かたわら is for two parallel ongoing occupations, not a single combined formal visit.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 散歩がてら

items.q: 散歩（ ）立ち寄った美術館は、とてもすいていた。
items.qr: Sanpo (___) tachiyotta bijutsukan wa, totemo suite ita.
items.en: The art museum I dropped by while out for a walk was very uncrowded.

opts.en: (not a valid combination — そばから attaches to verbs, not nouns this way)

items.why: Combining a walk with a museum visit is exactly Point 3's がてら; のそばから isn't a valid grammatical combination here.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 散歩がてら

items.q: その小説家は執筆（ ）、趣味でピアノを弾いている。
items.qr: Sono shousetsuka wa shippitsu (___), shumi de piano o hiite iru.
items.en: That novelist plays the piano as a hobby alongside their writing.

opts.en: while doing (wrong — piano isn't incidental to one trip/errand)

items.why: Writing and piano-playing are two ongoing life activities, not a single combined errand — Point 2's かたわら; がてら is for a one-off trip combining two purposes.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 6 · 散歩がてら

items.q: その商品は、並べる（ ）飛ぶように売れていった。
items.qr: Sono shouhin wa, naberu (___) tobu you ni urete itta.
items.en: That product sold like crazy the moment it was put on the shelf.

opts.en: while also (wrong — no two ongoing roles here)

items.why: Products selling out the instant they're shelved (a repeated, immediate cause-effect) is exactly Point 1's そばから.

items.q: （ ）店を続ける気はないです。
items.qr: (___) mise o tsuzukeru ki wa nai desu.
items.en: I have no intention of continuing to run the store even at the cost of taking a loss.

opts.en: although it's a loss (wrong — doesn't match the "willing to go this far" sense)
even if it's a loss (wrong register/fit for this structure)
(wrong — までも needs the て-form, not する directly)
even to the point of taking a loss

items.why: Week 3 Day 1's てまでも needs the て-form (して) before までも, describing the drastic length (a financial loss) one is unwilling to go to.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 普段着はシンプルで（ ）。
items.qr: Fudangi wa shinpuru de (___).
items.en: For everyday clothes, simple and durable is best.

opts.en: (wrong — 限りだ is for emotional adjectives, not "durable")
not limited to being durable (wrong sense entirely)
(wrong — this isn't a "not unique to X" claim)

items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 病気（ ）、いつまでも仕事を休んではいられない。
items.qr: Byouki (___), itsu made mo shigoto o yasunde wa irarenai.
items.en: Even though I'm sick, I can't keep taking time off work forever.

opts.en: needless to say (wrong — doesn't fit as a concession)
thought that... (wrong — no reversed expectation here)

items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: その商品がヒットしたの（ ）、次々と類似品が発売された。
items.qr: Sono shouhin ga hitto shita no (___), tsugitsugi to ruijihin ga hatsubai sareta.
items.en: Starting with that product's hit, similar products were released one after another.

opts.en: once ~, inevitably (wrong — no unstoppable habit here)
the moment (wrong — this needs a plain verb form, not a noun-marked event)

items.why: A hit product triggering a growing series of imitators is exactly Week 3 Day 4's を皮切りに.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 近くまで来ましたので、ご挨拶（ ）お伺いしました。
items.qr: Chikaku made kimashita node, go-aisatsu (___) oukagai shimashita.
items.en: Since I was nearby, I came to visit, combined with paying my respects.

opts.en: while also (wrong — no two ongoing life-roles)
while (wrong — too casual/simultaneous for this greeting)

items.why: Week 3 Day 6's かたがた is the standard formal-visit phrase combining a greeting with the act of dropping by.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 明日（ ）、退職いたします。
items.qr: Ashita (___), taishoku itashimasu.
items.en: As of tomorrow, I will retire.

opts.en: for the entire duration of (wrong — this is a single cutoff point, not a duration)

items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: デパートが開店する（ ）、主婦たちが特売場に押し寄せた。
items.qr: Depaato ga kaiten suru (___), shufutachi ga tokubaijou ni oshiyoseta.
items.en: No sooner had the department store opened than housewives rushed to the sale floor.

opts.en: immediately undone (wrong — opening isn't "undone," just followed by a rush)

items.why: A quick, almost simultaneous reaction (housewives rushing in) to a trigger (the store opening) is Week 3 Day 5's が早いか.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: （ ）と思っていたことだったが、記録しておいてよかった。
items.qr: (___) to omotte ita koto datta ga, kiroku shite oite yokatta.
items.en: I had thought there was no need to even write it down, but it was good that I recorded it.

opts.en: (wrong — downplays something already done, not a future need)

items.why: Week 3 Day 1's までもない dismisses writing as unnecessary — until the outcome (glad it was recorded) proved that assumption wrong.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 語彙を勉強しているが、覚えたと思った（ ）忘れてしまう。
items.qr: Goi o benkyou shite iru ga, oboeta to omotta (___) wasurete shimau.
items.en: I'm studying vocabulary, but no sooner do I think I've memorized it than I forget it.

opts.en: combined with (wrong — not a formal visit)
while also (wrong — not two ongoing roles)
while doing (wrong — not a two-purpose trip)

items.why: Memorization being instantly undone by forgetting is exactly Week 3 Day 6's そばから.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: この3週間（ ）、ろくに寝ていない。
items.qr: Kono san-shuukan (___), roku ni nete inai.
items.en: For these entire three weeks, I haven't slept properly.

opts.en: even ~ (wrong — a concession, not a duration marker)

items.why: An unbroken continuous state (poor sleep) across a named period is Week 3 Day 4's というもの.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: とにかくやってみよう。できなければ、あきらめる（ ）。
items.qr: Tonikaku yatte miyou. Dekinakereba, akirameru (___).
items.en: Anyway, let's try it. If it doesn't work, that just means giving up, nothing more.

opts.en: no need to even (wrong — giving up isn't being dismissed as unnecessary)
that's all there is to it

items.why: Week 3 Day 1's まで（のこと）だ downplays giving up as simply the natural, unremarkable consequence if the attempt fails.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼が美人で若いお嫁さんをもらったとは、うらやましい（ ）。
items.qr: Kare ga bijin de wakai oyomesan o moratta towa, urayamashii (___).
items.en: The fact that he got a beautiful young wife is envious in the extreme.

opts.en: (wrong — negates the intensity, opposite of intended meaning)
is the best (wrong — not a recommendation)

items.why: Week 3 Day 2's 限りだ intensifies envy to its peak, matching とは's exclamatory opening.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 遊びがてら（ ）。
items.qr: Asobi gatera (___).
items.en: Please do come by whenever you're out and about.

opts.en: please study well (wrong tone — doesn't match a casual "drop by" invitation)

opts.t: 看護師の勉強をしています
opts.r: kangoshi no benkyou o shite imasu

opts.t: ぜひいらっしゃってください

opts.en: (unrelated — this would need かたがた, not がてら)

items.why: 遊びがてら sets up a casual invitation (matching the book's own example, 遊びがてらお立ち寄りください) — only option 3 continues naturally as an invitation to visit.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 彼女は子どもを育てるかたわら、（ ）。
items.qr: Kanojo wa kodomo o sodateru katawara, (___).
items.en: While raising her children, she also runs a cooking class at home.

opts.t: 時間が足りなくて悩んでいる
opts.en: (a complaint, not a second ongoing role)

opts.t: 家で料理教室も開いている
opts.r: ie de ryouri kyoushitsu mo hiraite iru
opts.en: also runs a cooking class at home

opts.t: 家事が得意で何をするのも早い
opts.r: kaji ga tokui de nani o suru no mo hayai
opts.en: (a personality trait, not a second role)

opts.t: 将来は教師の資格を生かしたいそうだ
opts.r: shourai wa kyoushi no shikaku o ikashitai sou da
opts.en: (a future hope, not a current ongoing activity)

items.why: かたわら needs a genuinely separate ongoing secondary activity, matching the pattern's own example structure (running a shop alongside farming) — only option 2 names a real second occupation happening now.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 今日の試合に負けたといえども、（ ）。
items.qr: Kyou no shiai ni maketa to ie domo, (___).
items.en: Even though we lost today's match, there was almost no gap in strength between us and the other team.

opts.t: 勝つわけがないと思っていた
opts.r: katsu wake ga nai to omotte ita
opts.en: (contradicts といえども's concessive redeeming point)

opts.t: 勝てなかったのは仕方がなかった
opts.r: katenakatta no wa shikata ga nakatta
opts.en: (plausible, but doesn't redeem/qualify the loss as strongly)

opts.r: aite chiimu to no chikara no sa wa hotondo nakatta
opts.en: the gap in strength was almost nonexistent

opts.r: aite chiimu hodo no jitsuryoku wa nakatta
opts.en: (contradicts the redeeming point — admits being weaker)

items.why: といえども concedes the loss while still asserting something that softens/redeems it — option 3 asserts the teams were nearly evenly matched despite the loss, the classic "even though X, still Y holds" shape.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: ダイエットを成功させるのが難しいと感じているのは、私に（ ）だろう。
items.why: Week 3 Day 2's に限ったことではない — the difficulty isn't unique to the writer.

items.why: Week 3 Day 2's を限りに marks today as the intended cutoff point for eating sweets.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 健康を害する恐れもあるということは（ ）。

items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 理想の体重になった（ ）、リバウンドすることもよくあるからだ。

opts.en: the instant (plausible, but や否や flows more naturally into a habitual からだ clause)
thought that... (wrong — no stated expectation being reversed)

items.q: 結局（ ）、適度な運動をしてカロリーを消費したり、筋肉をつけることが大切だ。

opts.t: 毎日とはいかないまでも

opts.en: even every day (wrong — doesn't lower a bar, contradicts context)
for the entire duration of every day (wrong — redundant/nonsensical here)

items.why: Week 3 Day 1's ないまでも (here as the natural collocation とはいかないまでも) concedes that daily exercise may not be realistic, while still recommending moderate exercise as the achievable minimum.
items.unit: Week 3 Day 7 · 実戦問題

items.q: 何を買う（ ）、デパートの中をぶらぶらしていたら、友人に会った。

items.en: I was wandering around the department store without any particular thing to buy in mind, and I ran into a friend.

opts.en: without doing (wrong — needs a condition, not aimless browsing)

items.en: Without a healthy body, no matter how much money you have, you can't call yourself happy.

items.qr: Ano you na ichiryuu resutoran (___) to, dansei wa nekutai ga hitsuyou da.

items.why: Tax evasion involving the entire company (not just one person) is Point 3's ぐるみ — collective, often complicit, involvement.

items.qr: Natsu no kaigan de suna (___) ni natte asonda.
items.en: I played on the summer beach until I was covered in sand.

items.why: Being physically covered in sand while playing is Point 2's まみれ.

items.qr: Jouhou ga hanran suru jidai (___), hitsuyou na mono o sentaku suru no wa muzukashii.
items.en: In an era overflowing with information, it's difficult to choose what's necessary.

items.q: 「鈴木」なんていう名前、この町に千から（ ）んだよ。どうやって彼を探すんだよ。

items.qr: Sanbyaku-mai (___) CD no okiba ni komatte iru.

items.why: 枚 (a counter for flat objects like CDs) is a count/number, which takes からある, not からする (reserved for prices).

items.qr: Sakura no ki no shita de sake o nonde uta o utau. Nihon (___) ohanami no fuukei da.
items.en: Drinking and singing under the cherry blossoms — a scene of flower-viewing unique to Japan.

items.q: その若者と話してみて、多少（ ）共感できることがあった。
items.qr: Sono wakamono to hanashite mite, tashou (___) kyoukan dekiru koto ga atta.
items.en: After talking with that young person, there were things I could relate to, at least to some extent.

items.qr: Okane to jikan o kakereba, watashi ni datte sore wa dekinai (___).
items.en: If I put in enough money and time, it's not impossible for me to do that either.

items.why: Leaving open a real possibility given enough resources is Point 2's ないものでもない; ものか is an entirely different, much stronger rhetorical-denial pattern (not covered this week).
